tables.markdown:
| What memory has to answer | In one sentence | Which session supplies the evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Find the right target | Which cluster and which version does the retrieved experience belong to? | Neo4j's CrabRAG |
| Get corrections into the next retrieval | When a claim later turns out to be overstated, where does the fix go so it does not stop at the original document? | Agent Memory's consolidation and lifecycle |
| Connect conclusions back to observations | What exactly did "upgrade successful" observe? | NexaScience / RIKEN's verification of autonomous research |

| Type | Upgrade example | When it is updated | Who confirms it |
|---|---|---|---|
| working memory (what is currently loaded) | "assess the production cluster this time" | Released when the task ends; decisions and evidence needed for handoff or audit are kept separately | The owner of this task |
| episodic memory (a particular event and how it unfolded) | "last time the test cluster was upgraded to 1.31 and service A passed its health check" | Never rewritten; only corrections or withdrawals are added, with the time and environment attached | The platform engineer who checks observations |
| semantic memory (a fact that needs maintaining) | "service A in production now uses C version 3" | Updated whenever someone changes the configuration; the old value leaves the currently valid set | The owner of the configuration |
| procedural memory (a reusable step) | "check the actual plugin and its compatibility document before upgrading" | Its conditions of applicability are written with it; a revised procedure keeps a version | The procedure maintainer |

| Record | Claim | Requirement version and observations | Status and relationships |
|---|---|---|---|
| Old judgment J-17 | All of service A's required functions passed acceptance on 1.31 | Requirement v3 (version reached, health check, nightly report); cites observations O-41, node version 1.31, and O-42, health check passed; no report observation | Withdrawn, because the report was paused during the rehearsal and was consolidated as passed without any result |
| New judgment J-18 | The test cluster reached 1.31 and service A passed its health check; the report job has not yet been accepted | Requirement v3; cites O-41 and O-42; marks the missing verification of the report's run and output | Valid; supersedes J-17; confirmed by the service owner |
| Derived summary P-9 | The upgrade plan copied J-17's conclusion, "service A can be upgraded to 1.31" | Based on J-17 | Not valid grounds until rebuilt; after the rebuild it cites J-18 instead |

| How the memory relates to current data | What the one taking over should do | What the acceptance reviewer examines |
|---|---|---|
| Target, version, and requirements match; source can be checked | Use the experience to narrow the investigation, and obtain the current evidence still needed | Cited sources, necessary queries, and items still to be confirmed |
| The old result came from a different environment | Treat it as a lead, and reconfirm the conditions of this environment | Whether a cross-environment inference was written up as a verified fact |
| The old conclusion has been corrected by new evidence | Retrieve the correction relationship, and adjust the recommendation to the new evidence | Whether the original text, summaries, and search entry points still push the outdated conclusion |
| The primary record has been withdrawn, but the index or derived summaries have not yet been rebuilt | Do not treat the old summary as currently valid grounds; report that a correction is in progress | Whether the query layer holds back the old conclusion, rather than relying on a flag alone |
| Two sources conflict, and the data to tell them apart is missing | Preserve the dispute, and identify who needs to supply which data | Whether it took sides on its own based on occurrence count or update time |
| Content has been deleted under the retention rules | Do not re-supply the content through summaries, indexes, or exported copies | Each copy that needs clearing, and the actual search results |
| The same question is asked by a role without read access | The data service restricts what is retrieved according to the current role | Tool responses, content loaded into the model, and the final answer |

| Field | Content for this case |
|---|---|
| Task and target | Production cluster prod-a, service A, target 1.31; read access only |
| Original requirement | The same acceptance checklist v3, including the nightly report |
| Existing observations | Version reached, health check passed; no report result |
| Conclusions allowed after the correction | Two items confirmed, report pending; not yet enough to claim all required functions passed |
| Forbidden conclusions | All required functions passed; the report is known to be incompatible |
| Propagation acceptance | Neither a normal query nor a summary rebuild can restore J-17 |
| Human exits | Who may suspend the use of the old conclusion, who approves the replacement judgment, who takes over when the owner is away |

assets.caption: Shibuya at night on September 11, 2026. The observation deck, the city lights, and the low clouds are all kept in one frame. Photograph by the author.
Stephen Chin / Neo4j, deck page 28: a friend, a preferred food, and the place it is found, joined by named relationships into a path that can be queried. Source: official slides.

Rohit Ghumare and Vinuja Khatode, deck page 11: current task content, how events unfolded, extracted facts, and reusable steps each carry a different memory job. Source: full-page rendering of the official PPTX.

Agent Memory deck, page 28: a memory can be reinforced, replaced by a new version, downweighted, or deleted; sources and version history need retention rules of their own. Source: full-page rendering of the official PPTX.
Wataru Kumagai / NexaScience and RIKEN, deck page 35: decide how a claim will be verified before producing the results. Source: official slides.

The venue as photographed by the author on September 10, 2026, corresponding to page 40 of Wataru Kumagai's deck: the research system submits material, the verifier records a judgment, and the paper is produced from verified claims. Slide content: NexaScience / RIKEN; photograph by the author.
Lanterns and exhibition signage at SHIBUYA SKY's "天空夢祭" on the evening of September 11, 2026. Photograph by the author.
